age.evidence: 18 adult male Long Evans rats (Envigo, Indianapolis, IN) (350-375 g)

sex.evidence: 18 adult male Long Evans rats (Envigo, Indianapolis, IN) (350-375 g)

dosing.doses_raw: psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p., Sigma-Aldrich); one rat received 0.33 mg/kg instead of 1 mg/kg of psilocybin
dosing.evidence: the Psilocybin group was administered a single dose of psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.) and the Vehicle group 1 ml/kg of vehicle (saline).

handling.evidence: all rats were handled, for at least three days, and then habituated to the operant chambers and trained in the DDT

group_housing.evidence: pair-housed in standard polycarbonate cages (45 x 24 x 20 cm)

day_night_flipped.evidence: on a 12 hours light/dark cycle (lights on at 9:00 P.M.)... All experiments were performed during the dark phase when the animals are most active.

assays.assay_description: Rats injected with vehicle or psilocybin (1 mg/kg i.p.) and immediately placed in acrylic boxes (16" W x 16" D x 15" H), video recorded for 60 min; two blinded observers live-counted head twitches per 5-min bins.

application_type.evidence: rats received a single injection of vehicle (saline, 1 ml/kg, i.p.) or psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p., Sigma-Aldrich)

setup_habituation.evidence: rats were taken to a procedural room and acclimated for 30 min. Then, rats were injected... and then immediately placed in acrylic boxes (room acclimation only, no apparatus pre-exposure described)

setup_restrain.evidence: immediately placed in acrylic boxes (16" W x 16" D x 15" H) and video recorded for 60 min using a camera positioned above the box

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the acrylic boxes during recording

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the acrylic boxes during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: Head-twitch responses for 60 min were assessed immediately after injections.

sample_size.evidence: Vehicle (n= 8) and Psilocybin (n= 8)... two rats were not injected with psilocybin... t(12)= 10.14; Figure 5: Vehicle (n = 8) and Psilocybin (n = 6)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (1 mg/kg i.p.) increased total head-twitch responses over 60 min versus vehicle (5.33 ± 0.54 vs 0.5 ± 0.2). The effect was maximal 10 min after administration and returned to baseline by 60 min.
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin increased the total number of head-twitch responses in 60 min compared to vehicle (Vehicle= 0.5 ±0.2; Psilocybin= 5.33 ±0.54; t(12)= 10.14. p< 0.001). This effect was maximal 10 min after administration and returned to baseline after 60 min.

B1_num_measures.evidence: the total number of head-twitch responses in 60 min

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: live counted the number of head twitches per 5 min time stamps... This effect was maximal 10 min after administration and returned to baseline after 60 min.

B4_ethological.evidence: head-twitch response is excluded as ethological per rubric

B5_social.evidence: rats tested individually in acrylic boxes

B6_cognitive.evidence: HTR does not require learning or memory

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Two trained observers blind to treatment live counted the number of head twitches

B8_multivariate.evidence: A Student independent t test was used to evaluate the effects of psilocybin on head twitch responses

E1_environment_type.evidence: acrylic boxes (16" W x 16" D x 15" H)

E6_spatial.evidence: acrylic boxes (16" W x 16" D x 15" H)

E7_social_context.evidence: rats were... immediately placed in acrylic boxes and video recorded

D3_recording_days.evidence: Head-twitch responses for 60 min were assessed immediately after injections

D4_baseline.evidence: acclimated for 30 min without data collection; no pre-drug HTR baseline reported

D5_followup.evidence: HTR assessed only immediately after injection

assays.assay_description: Coulbourn operant chamber with two retractable levers and food trough; free-choice and forced-choice trials between small immediate (1 pellet) and large delayed (3 pellets; 1, 10, 20 s delays) rewards; 3 blocks x 20 trials (<60 min sessions). Baseline (last training sessions) and tests 24 h and 48 h after psilocybin/vehicle. Measures: LR choices, SR choices, choice latency, correct and incorrect forced-choice responses, forced-choice latency, omissions.

application_type.evidence: the Psilocybin group was administered a single dose of psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: all rats were handled, for at least three days, and then habituated to the operant chambers and trained in the DDT

setup_restrain.evidence: sound attenuated operant chamber with two retractable levers (right and left) and a food trough; freely moving apparatus

food_restriction.evidence: Pressing the LR lever delivered 3 sugar pellets while pressing the SR delivered 1 sugar pellet (pellets available during session; rats also on mild chronic diet: 'mild food-restricted diet (15 g of chow per rat and day)')

water_restriction.evidence: no water described in the operant chamber

time_to_assay.evidence: Then, 24 and 48 hours after psilocybin or vehicle injections, both groups of rats were tested in the DDT.

sample_size.evidence: Vehicle (n= 8) and Psilocybin (n= 8)... two rats were not injected with psilocybin; group: F(1,12); Figure 5: Vehicle (n = 8) and Psilocybin (n = 6)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin decreased LR choices (group trend p=0.054; significant at 10 s delay 48 h) and increased latency to LR choices (p=0.041; session-dependent, significant at 20 s delay 48 h), without changing SR choices or omissions; forced-choice accuracy decreased only at 20 s delay at 48 h. Effects emerged at 48 h but not 24 h and were delay-independent, interpreted as reduced reward seeking rather than altered impulsivity.
outcomes.statistics: LR choices: group F(1,12)=4.58, p=0.054, ηp2=0.27; 10 s delay 48 h p=0.026, ηp2=0.35. Choice latency: group F(1,8)=5.94, p=0.041, ηp2=0.43; session x group F(1,8)=9.59, p=0.015, ηp2=0.54; 20 s delay 48 h p=0.006, ηp2=0.63. Accuracy: group F(1,12)=1.17, p=0.30; session x delay x group F(2,24)=3.42, p=0.049; 20 s delay 48 h p=0.026. Forced latency: group F(1,9)=0.176, p=0.68. SR choices: group F(1,12)=0.01, p=0.901. Omissions: group F(1,12)=2.93, p=0.112.
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin decreased the number of LR choices compared to vehicle, although this effect did not reach statistical significance (group: F(1,12)= 4.58, p= 0.054)... planned comparisons demonstrated that this decrease was significant at 10 s delay 48 hours after psilocybin injections (p= 0.026)... psilocybin increased the latency to LR choices compared to vehicle (group: F(1,8)= 5.94, p= 0.041)

B1_num_measures.evidence: LR choice, SR choice, accuracy (i.e., number of correct and incorrect responses in forced choice trials), latency and omissions; choice latency and forced-choice latency reported separately

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: session-level values per delay block; no within-session time-course analysis

B5_social.evidence: rats tested individually in operant chambers

B6_cognitive.evidence: Rats were trained in a delay discounting task (DDT) where rats chose between delayed large rewards (LR) and immediate small rewards (SR)

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Coulbourn operant chamber lever-press recording; no ML behavioural classification

B8_multivariate.evidence: Two- and three-way ANOVAs with repeated measures; separate univariate tests

E1_environment_type.evidence: sound attenuated operant chamber with two retractable levers

E6_spatial.evidence: operant chamber with levers and food trough in the same wall

E7_social_context.evidence: rats tested individually in operant chambers

E8_food_water.evidence: Pressing the LR lever delivered 3 sugar pellets while pressing the SR delivered 1 sugar pellet. The pellet/s were delivered to the food trough

D1_continuity.evidence: Rats were tested in the DDT 24 and 48 hours after psilocybin injections; baseline training sessions also analysed

D2_session_duration.evidence: The task consisted of 3 blocks of 20 trials each (60 trials total, < 60 min sessions)

D3_recording_days.evidence: no differences in large reward (LR) choices among the last six training sessions... 24 and 48 hours after psilocybin or vehicle injections, both groups of rats were tested in the DDT

D4_baseline.evidence: Figure 3, Figure 4 and supplemental Figure 1 display the effects of psilocybin... 24 and 48 hours after injections compared to baseline (before psilocybin injections)

D5_followup.evidence: Rats were tested in the DDT 24 and 48 hours after psilocybin injections

judge_notes: All candidates identified the same two assays (HTR and DDT); immunohistochemistry excluded as non-behavioural.
HTR B1 set to score 0 (single measure) overriding gemma4's score of 1, which was inconsistent with its value '1'.
HTR setup_habituation set to not_reported overriding modal 'yes': the 30-min acclimation was to the procedural room, not the acrylic box apparatus (room acclimation excluded by rubric).
DDT B1 set to 7+ (score 3): LR choice, SR choice, choice latency, correct responses, incorrect responses, forced-choice latency, omissions are reported separately.
DDT D3 set to 8-14 (modal): last six baseline training sessions were analysed plus 24 h and 48 h tests.
DDT D5 set to Yes (modal; gemma4's 'No' contradicts the 24/48 h post-injection testing).
DDT food_restriction set to 'no' (modal): pellets delivered during sessions; mild chronic 15 g/day diet noted in evidence as a weight-maintenance protocol.
Sample size n_total=14 (Vehicle 8, Psilocybin 6) based on t(12)/F(1,12) df and Figure 5 legend; two rats were not injected.
